dc_queue.source_cadence: ISO-published DC-load queue, Depth Master Shell

dc_queue_measured.source_cadence: DC Hub's own row-level classification of the interconnection queue

fuel_mix.source_cadence: EIA hourly RTO fuel mix — published several hours behind demand; an overnight reading is routinely 18-24h old

lmp.source_cadence: ISO real-time LMP (5-min) via iso_lmp_snapshots / gridstatus ISO-NE

load_forecast.source_cadence: gridstatus.io via the Grid Data Master Shell, which ingests ONE dataset per daily tick across a ~22-entry registry — a given category refreshes on the order of weeks. Read age_minutes, not the label.

telemetry.source_cadence: DC Hub ISO telemetry poll (~1.5h cron)

freshness_sla.note: Ages computed at response time from each layer's source timestamp. Every promoted extended metric has a layer here — if a field is in the payload and NOT in layers, its age is unknown and it is listed in unaged_layers. Cross-check the public SLA endpoint — no tracked rival exposes verifiable data age.

unaged_layers.reason: no parseable source timestamp — treat the value as of UNKNOWN age

generation_mix_freshness_basis: generation_mix_age_hours and generation_mix_stale_hours are measured against the CURRENT UTC clock at request time. generation_mix_lag_at_snapshot_hours is the feed-to-feed lag inside the snapshot (demand_period − generation_mix_period) and is ALWAYS smaller — it excludes the snapshot's own age. Before 2026-08-05 generation_mix_stale_hours carried that smaller lag and under-reported true age.
generation_mix_note: Fuel mix is EIA's latest PUBLISHED hour (2026-10-24T04), which is ~22.2h old as of right now. It also trails the demand reading (2026-10-25T01) by ~21h, because EIA publishes the fuel-type breakdown slower than aggregate demand. Treat the mix / renewable + gas shares as a snapshot from 2026-10-24T04, NOT the current minute's mix — do not narrate it as "right now". demand_mw is the fresher reading.

headroom_measured.adjustment_method: Documented measurement artifact: ERCOT gen feed (seMW) is gross generation (+13pp of load); MISO online gen excludes imports (−14pp). Raw telemetry is stored unmodified; the adjustment is applied at serving, both values shown.
headroom_measured.basis: measured (ISO telemetry gen − demand), not modeled

headroom_unavailable.note: No ISO-level substation headroom is published here: the headroom estimator works from a point (lat/lon) and does not place an ISO, so its substations are not shown for a region they are not in. For a site, use get_grid_data or analyze_site with coordinates; for the ISO queue, see /api/v1/interconnection-queue/snapshot.

note: EIA hourly RTO data via api.eia.gov/v2/electricity/rto.

caveats.text: EIA-930 hourly values are collected as reported by the balancing authorities and published in real time, so they can be anomalous and are corrected later by EIA; DC Hub serves the latest settled hour.

min_mw.method: minimum of the settled hourly demand points in the 24h series

peak_mw.method: maximum of the settled hourly demand points in the 24h series

provenance.method: realtime EIA generation mix + demand, assembled per region (5-min cache); as_of = the oldest period among the labelled figures
provenance.source: EIA-930 hourly RTO/BA feed (MISO) + DC Hub grid intelligence
